newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank denies rumours on baht controls.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank denies rumours on baht controls.

text.p: Thailand's central bank on Friday denied rumours in the foreign exchange market that its latest currency controls to defend the baht from offshore speculators would be lifted soon.

"The Bank of Thailand wishes to deny market rumours that the restrictions on offshore baht will be lifted. The measures implemented by the Bank of Thailand to restrict the supply of baht in the offshore market will remain firmly in place in its totality," a Bank of Thailand statement said.
The central bank in mid-May imposed the controls to restrict baht outflows in order to squeeze speculators who had attacked the currency earlier.
The move created a two-tier market where the baht was traded higher offshore than onshore.
Rumours circulated in the market this morning that the authorities would soon remove the controls, prompting the baht to slide in offshore markets.
Following the central bank's denial, the offshore baht firmed to 24.150/24.350 per dollar against 24.550/24.650 earlier, dealers said.
